clue.text: Support scout group wanting to travel cheaply

parts.note: to support someone is to back them
a pack is a group of Cub Scouts

explanation.surface: Someone hopes their scout troop will fund a budget trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' is a link here, not part of either piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To backpack is to roam on a budget carrying all your kit in a rucksack, so it is travelling cheaply.

parts.note: Dracula can turn into a flying mammal of the night, so his man would be named after that creature; the term is also an army officer's orderly

explanation.walkthrough: The British army term is for an officer's personal orderly; the cryptic reading gives the vampire, who changes into a bat, his own man.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a military officer's orderly, and punningly a servant to the vampire who becomes a bat.

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the troubles word wraps around the letter I

parts.note: troubles or worries are cares

explanation.surface: Someone laments that their many worries are wearing them down.
explanation.definitionFit: Caries is the medical term for tooth or bone decay.

clue.text: Cushion for army captive with internal injury

indicators.note: with internal says the second piece sits within the first one

parts.note: POW is a prisoner of war, a captive soldier
ill can be a noun meaning harm or injury

explanation.surface: A cushion is provided for a wounded prisoner of war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'army captive' suggests a soldier, but it is the abbreviation for a prisoner of war.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillow is a soft cushion for resting the head on in bed.

clue.text: Talk with a woman — the lady of the house

parts.note: to talk casually is to chat
Elaine is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A conversation with a woman who turns out to be the mistress of the household.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatelaine is the mistress of a large house or castle, who keeps its keys.

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
to sup is to drink, in sips

explanation.surface: A tomcat laps at a drink and some sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' and 'and' are links joining the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Catsup is a variant spelling of ketchup, a tomato sauce used as a condiment.

clue.text: Just the marine to deploy round California

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Just the marine to deploy round California', gives AMERI(CA)N from an anagram of MARINE round CA, but 'Just the' cannot define AMERICAN: the definition word looks misread by OCR and no source gives the printed clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Just the marine to deploy round California

clue.text: Very little lad catches little fly

indicators.note: catches means the lad word holds the fly word inside it

parts.note: a lad is a boy, a son
a midge is a small fly

explanation.surface: A tiny boy grabs at a small insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgeon is a very small amount, a tiny bit of something.

parts.note: a port is a harbour
rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: A painter captures the lamps of a harbour at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray something is to depict it in art or words.

parts.note: a tyro is a beginner or novice
lean means thin, with little fat on the body

explanation.surface: A slim beginner from Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrolean means from the Tyrol, an Alpine region in western Austria.

clue.text: He doesn't believe it's of material weight

definitions.meaning: one who denies something, refusing to believe it
a unit measuring the fineness of yarn or fabric such as nylon stockings, by weight per length

explanation.walkthrough: 'it's of' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A denier is one who denies, and also a unit of weight per length used to grade fibres and hosiery.

indicators.note: arranging tells us to put these letters into a new order, as one arranges a vase

explanation.surface: A florist tells someone to watch nobody else do the floral display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranging' shuffles SEENOMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Anemones are spring flowers of the buttercup family, also called windflowers.

definitions.meaning: Geri Halliwell's nickname in the pop group the Spice Girls, who later left
mettle or liveliness, as in putting some energy into something

explanation.walkthrough: 'displays' links the two definitions. The Spice Girls were a 1990s British pop group whose members had nicknames.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger Spice was Geri Halliwell's stage name, and the word also means spirit or vigour.

clue.text: To study physics perhaps requires scruples

parts.note: to con is an old word for studying or learning by heart
physics is an example of a science, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone notes that studying physics demands moral care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requires' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscience is the inner moral sense that gives one scruples.

clue.text: Workshop held by a Socialist or a Conservative

parts.note: Lab is short for Labour, the UK socialist party
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A workshop occupied by either a left-wing or a right-wing politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' is a link. 'or' and the second 'a' are taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory is a room or building for scientific work, a working space like a workshop.

indicators.note: tortured means twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A resistance fighter is tortured in the ancient Greek city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tortured' shuffles INSPARTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a member of an armed resistance group fighting occupiers.

clue.text: Be proud to be in opposition

definitions.meaning: proud in its sense of sticking out from a surface, as a nail head might
to resist firmly or refuse to give in

explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links the definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand out is to project, i.e. be proud of a surface, and also to hold out against something.

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at an unexpected arrangement, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A naval rating turns out not to be uneducated after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' shuffles NORATING; a rating is a naval sailor, so the surface sounds naval.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant means lacking education or knowledge, so unschooled.

indicators.note: dire means dreadful, suggesting the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A hostile man's enmity brings everything to a dreadful halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dire' shuffles STAGNATION; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An antagonist is an opponent whose hostility obstructs others, so the whole clue fits.

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a degree held by an educated person
a Scot lives in the north of Britain

explanation.surface: A well-schooled man from the north is charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a lucky charm or talisman.

clue.text: Motor round Roman road to find fine food

indicators.note: round says the motor word goes around the road word

parts.note: a motor is a car
via is Latin for road, as in the Via Appia

explanation.surface: Someone drives around Roman roads hunting gourmet fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviar, salted sturgeon roe, is a classic luxury delicacy.

definitions.meaning: people who sew, read with a different pronunciation

explanation.walkthrough: 'used by' links the two definitions; the word is said differently in each sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewers are waste drains, and also people who sew, like seamstresses.

clue.text: Can get tea container of inferior quality

parts.note: a can is a tin
a teapot holds tea

explanation.surface: A can is being used as a teapot, a shoddy arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot is an informal adjective meaning shoddy, petty or second-rate.

clue.text: Father's home when Victor has a tantrum

parts.note: Vic is the short form of the name Victor
a tantrum is a fit of rage

explanation.surface: Dad's house is where Victor throws a fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' and 'has' are links. 'Father' is a priest here, not a dad.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicarage is a house provided for a vicar, a clergyman addressed as Father.

parts.note: slog is hard work or labour

explanation.surface: The Labour Party needs a catchy campaign line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is a link. Labour here is toil, not the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a short memorable phrase used in advertising.

indicators.note: organisation means arranging, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A lazy moral-crusade group does nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' shuffles ANTIVICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inactive means idle or not doing anything, close to indolent.

clue.text: Refusal by art gallery to use symbolic characters

parts.note: no is a refusal
the Tate is a group of art galleries in Britain, such as Tate Modern

explanation.surface: An art gallery declines to display symbols.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To notate is to write something down in a system of symbols, such as music notation.

definitions.meaning: highlights or presents as a main attraction
standing articles or columns in a newspaper or magazine

explanation.definitionFit: To feature something is to give it prominence, and features are regular articles in a publication.
